title: Superwall Alternatives for Indie iOS Apps
goal: Non-branded organic + AI-cited sessions; first earned citations
geoAnswerBlock: The practical Superwall alternatives for an indie iOS app are RevenueCat when purchase and entitlement infrastructure is the priority, Adapty when paywall analytics and experimentation should live together, and Qonversion when a lower percentage meter matters. For a simple Apple-only app, native StoreKit 2 may fit better than another platform.

factLedger.claim: Superwall's subscription infrastructure is free at any scale; its paywall product is free up to $10,000 monthly paywall-attributed revenue, then 1% of paywall-attributed revenue.
Superwall currently includes entitlements, purchase APIs, receipt validation, webhooks, analytics, SQL access, paywalls, and experiments.
RevenueCat is free up to $2,500 monthly tracked revenue, then charges 1% of tracked revenue.
RevenueCat models offerings and entitlements and can pair a remotely configured paywall with an offering.
Adapty is free under $5,000 monthly revenue, then charges 1% of monthly revenue.
Adapty offers remote paywall and flow configuration, A/B tests, and subscription analytics; new projects are directed to Flow Builder.
Qonversion is free up to $10,000 MTR; Starter is 0.6% of revenue; Growth is 0.8% and adds A/B experiments.
StoreKit 2 provides Swift APIs for products, transactions, entitlements, subscription state, and merchandising views.
The App Store Server API provides transaction history and current subscription status from a server.
RevenueCat and Superwall provide documented integration paths that keep RevenueCat as the purchase or entitlement source of truth while Superwall handles paywalls.

repurposing.hook: The cheapest Superwall alternative is not the tool with the lowest percentage. First ask what revenue the percentage measures.
Four exits from Superwall: purchase truth, analytics workflow, lower meter, or no platform.
Superwall is no longer only a paywall SDK. If that is why you plan to switch, update the premise before you update the code.

editorNotes: Replaced the brief's stale billing-suite versus paywall-SDK premise with the current category reality: the major products overlap, so the decision turns on center of gravity and pricing base.
Added the Qonversion tier distinction: the 0.6% Starter rate excludes A/B experiments, so Growth at 0.8% is the closer Superwall replacement.
Made the StoreKit-only case operationally honest: no third-party platform fee does not mean no engineering responsibility.
